Thinking through this as myself...

My land is 3.8 mu total. Chili is my main business — that's what I've been building up over the years. I'll put most of the land into chili, maybe 2.5 mu. The rest, about 1.3 mu, I'll plant maize. Maize is easy, my husband can manage it when he's between off-farm work. It also gives us grain for the household and feed if we keep animals.

For chili, I'll buy improved variety seeds from the county market — not the cheapest, but the yield is better and buyers pay more for the standard size. I've learned that skimping on seed money is a mistake. Chili eats fertilizer, especially nitrogen and potassium. I'll apply base fertilizer before transplanting, then top-dress twice during fruiting. Irrigation from the well is critical — I water about once every 10-15 days in the dry stretches, more during fruit set. Pests and disease (especially aphids and blight) are my biggest worry with chili, so I won't cut corners on spraying.

For maize, I always use hybrid seed — everyone in the village does, the yield difference is obvious. Maize is lower maintenance. A few irrigations, one or two pesticide sprays for corn borer, standard fertilizer. I do rotary tillage on both plots before planting.

With some family off-farm, I manage labor carefully — chili takes the most of my time from May through September.
